about.title: Westminster Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet floor in a grocery aisle. A crumbling curb stop in a parking lot off Beach Boulevard. A stairwell light that has been out for weeks at an apartment complex near Goldenwest Street. Falls like these happen quietly in Westminster all the time, and the people who get hurt often blame themselves first. California law looks at it differently. Property owners in Orange County have a duty to keep their premises reasonably safe. When they knew about a hazard, or should have caught it with ordinary care, and did nothing to fix or warn about it, they can be held responsible for the harm that followed. LawProactive exists to make the next step simple. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Westminster residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes premises liability cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you fell at a shop along Westminster Boulevard, in a rental unit, or on a public walkway, we can help you find someone to review what happened.

whyChoose.title: Why Westminster Residents Turn to LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys Who Understand the Notice Rule
items.desc: In California, a fall alone is not enough; you generally have to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. The attorneys in our network know how to build that part of the case from inspection logs, maintenance records and witness accounts.

items.title: Fast Help Preserving Video and Evidence
items.desc: Store and apartment surveillance footage is often overwritten within days. Getting connected quickly means an attorney can send a preservation request and gather photos of the hazard before it is repaired or erased.

items.title: Honest Guidance on Deadlines and Shared Fault
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, and it is far shorter when a public entity owns the property. Under pure comparative fault you can still recover even if you were partly to blame, and an attorney can explain how that applies to your situation.

items.question: I slipped inside a store on Beach Boulevard in Westminster and the manager said it was my fault. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly careless your recovery is reduced by your share of blame rather than eliminated. The bigger question is whether the store knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can request the store's sweep logs and camera footage to find out.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: Get medical care first, then document as much as you can: photos of the exact spot, the substance or defect, the lighting, and any missing warning signs. Ask for an incident report and the names of witnesses. If cameras are visible, note their location so an attorney can request the footage before it is deleted.

items.question: I fell on a public sidewalk in Westminster. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: Yes, and this matters a great deal. When a city, county or other public entity owns the property, California requires a government claim to be filed first, usually within six months of the injury, rather than the two years that applies to private owners. Because that window closes quickly, it is worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible.
